jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer - Vision Foundation Models
jobs.description:
The Perception team at Zoox is responsible for how our purpose-built robotaxi understands the world, including what happens inside the cabin. In this role, you will design, train, and evaluate vision-based in-cabin perception models that understand passengers, objects, and behaviors inside the vehicle. These models support rider safety and the operations that keep each ride running smoothly.

You will independently own a model area end to end, from data curation and training through evaluation and deployment under real-time and compute constraints, working closely with partners across the company. Your work has a direct impact on rider safety and experience as Zoox scales its robotaxi service.

### **In this role, you will...**

* Design, train, and evaluate vision models that understand passengers, objects, and behaviors inside the vehicle, across detection, pose, and action recognition.
* Independently own a model or feature area end to end: curate data, define labeling guidelines, train and evaluate models, and take them through deployment.
* Set the quality bar for the models you own, using rigorous evaluation and error analysis so they are reliable enough to support live operations.
* Deploy models under real-time and compute constraints shared with the rest of the onboard perception system.
* Partner across product, operations, safety, and vehicle software to turn requirements into model specifications, metrics, and validation plans.

### **Qualifications**

* MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, or a related field with 6+ years of industry experience (PhD with 3+ years).
* Deep expertise in computer vision and deep learning for image and video understanding: object detection, pose and action recognition, and fine-grained classification, with hands-on experience with modern architectures (convolutional and vision-transformer detectors, and self-supervised or foundation-model backbones such as DINOv3).
* Strong proficiency in Python and PyTorch for model design, training, and evaluation.
* Experience with vision-language models or foundation-model backbones, and with auto-labeling or synthetic data for long-tail and rare classes.
* Track record of owning the full ML lifecycle on real-world data: dataset curation and labeling guidelines, training, metric design (precision, recall, and false-positive rate at an operating point), and error analysis.

### **Bonus Qualifications**

* Experience with in-cabin or occupant monitoring (occupant or driver monitoring systems), ideally including multi-camera or fisheye imagery and low-light conditions.
* Experience deploying deep learning models to real-time, resource-constrained systems (robotics, automotive, or edge devices) with TensorRT / ONNX or similar.
* Proficiency in C++ for model integration.

**Base Salary Range**

There are three major components to compensation for this position: salary, Amazon Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights. A sign-on bonus may be offered as part of the compensation package. The listed range applies only to the base salary. Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level. Leveling, as well as positioning within a level, is determined by a range of factors, including, but not limited to, a candidate's relevant years of experience, domain knowledge, and interview performance. The salary range listed in this posting is representative of the range of levels Zoox is considering for this position.

Zoox also offers a comprehensive package of benefits, including paid time off (e.g. sick leave, vacation, bereavement), unpaid time off, Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights, Amazon RSUs, health insurance, long-term care insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance, and life insurance.

**About Zoox**

Zoox is developing the first ground-up, fully autonomous vehicle fleet and the supporting ecosystem required to bring this technology to market. Sitting at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and design, Zoox aims to provide the next generation of mobility-as-a-service in urban environments. We’re looking for top talent that shares our passion and wants to be part of a fast-moving and highly execution-oriented team.

jobs.description:
Apptronik is a human-centered robotics company developing AI-powered robots to support humanity in every facet of life. Our flagship humanoid robot, Apollo, is built to collaborate thoughtfully with people, starting with critical industries such as manufacturing and logistics, with future applications in healthcare, the home, and beyond.  
  
We operate at the cutting edge of Applied AI, applying our expertise across the full robotics stack to solve some of society's most important problems. You will join a team dedicated to bringing Apollo to market at scale, tackling the complex challenges like safety, commercialization, and mass production to change the world for the better.

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Software Engineer - Manipulation is a core contributor to our robot's ability to interact with the world reliably and precisely. This role is responsible for developing and deploying learning-based manipulation policies, with a focus on post-training methods that adapt and improve those policies on real tasks and physical hardware.

This role will bridge the gap between cutting-edge research and scalable, reliable production software. Working closely with the simulation, data, hardware, and systems teams, this engineer will take manipulation policies from demonstration data through post-training to robust deployment across our fleet.

  

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES or KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES**

* Implement and deploy state-of-the-art learning-based manipulation policies to achieve reliable, world-class performance on real-world tasks with physical hardware.
* Adapt and improve policies for new tasks and hardware using post-training methods such as RL fine-tuning, policy distillation, and interactive imitation learning (e.g., DAgger).
* Build and maintain the data pipelines that support post-training, including teleoperation and demonstration collection, retargeting, dataset aggregation, and curation.
* Drive the development cycle from simulation and offline evaluation to robustly transferring and fine-tuning policies on the robot.
* Develop visuomotor policies for grasping, in-hand manipulation, and whole-arm manipulation, with reliable, low-latency execution on hardware.
* Define evaluation metrics and regression tests for policy performance in simulation and on hardware, and use the results to guide technical decisions.
* Collaborate closely with the simulation, data, hardware, and systems teams to diagnose system-level issues and co-develop solutions.
* Maintain high standards for the codebase through testing, documentation, and peer code reviews.
  

**SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS**

**Technical Skills (Must-Have)**

* **Manipulation:** Strong experience in robotic manipulation, including grasping, in-hand or whole-arm control, and high-DOF motion, with a track record of hardware deployment.
* **Learning-Based Control:** Hands-on experience training and debugging learned policies, including post-training methods such as RL fine-tuning, distillation, and imitation learning (e.g., DAgger).

* **Computer Vision:** Familiarity with 6D pose estimation, point cloud processing, or visual-servoing.

* An MS with 3+ years of relevant experience, or a recent PhD, in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.

jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon Leo is closing the digital divide with a constellation of 3,236 low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites bringing fast, affordable broadband to communities the internet has never reliably reached. The customer terminal is the phased-array antenna at the customer's premises that turns that constellation into a working internet link — and our team writes the embedded software that makes it work: acquiring a LEO satellite on a fast overhead pass, electronically steering the beam to track it, closing and holding the link, and handing over to the next satellite within seconds. This is a broad role — you can work across the full signal chain and go deep wherever interests you most.  
  
What you'll work on:  

* Electronic beam steering & tracking — real-time control that keeps a phased-array beam pointed at a fast-moving satellite across the pass and through every handover.
* Phased-array calibration — per-element amplitude/phase calibration that holds beam and sidelobe performance across unit-to-unit variation, temperature, and frequency, on real hardware in the field, with the automated test coverage to keep it reliable.
* Link acquisition, tracking & management — satellite acquisition, closed-loop tracking, and the control that brings the link up, keeps it healthy, and reacquires cleanly through handovers.
* RF power & thermal management — managing transmit power and duty cycle against PA and platform thermal limits so the terminal runs at full performance without exceeding its envelope.
* System integration & field telemetry — integrate the RF front-end, controls, and signal path, then use device telemetry to debug and improve terminals operating on orbit.

Rust, C/C++, and Python on embedded Linux / RTOS, working directly with the RF front-end and real hardware — lab terminals, RF test benches, and satellites on orbit. jobs.description:
**About Etched**

Etched is building hardware for frontier intelligence. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing to deliver best-in-class throughput and latency across both prefill and decode workloads. Our first products are heavily focused on **inference**. Backed by hundreds of millions from top-tier investors and staffed by leading engineers, Etched is redefining the infrastructure layer for the fastest growing industry in history.

**Job Summary**

Etched is seeking a **Test Infrastructure Engineer** to build and run the infrastructure behind factory testing of our AI systems, from new product introduction through mass production.

You will join a new, small central team that owns making factory testing reliable, repeatable, and scalable. A factory test floor looks a lot like a small datacenter: hundreds of boards, servers, and racks under test at once, all running our test software and reporting results back. You will own that layer: the systems that provision and run test stations, move test results and logs into one reliable source of truth, and roll out new test software safely across factories. You will work closely with hardware, firmware, software, and production teams, and with our contract manufacturing partners.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Build and operate the test execution platform that runs factory tests across stations, servers, and racks, and keep it running reliably during factory hours.
* Provision and manage the Linux fleet on the factory floor: OS imaging and network boot, configuration management, and lifecycle automation for test stations and systems under test.
* Design and maintain the networking that test stations and racks depend on, working with factory partners on site.
* Build data pipelines that reliably capture every test run, its logs, and hardware genealogy into a central view of test history, yield, throughput, and unit history.
* Own versioned release, canary, and rollback of factory test packages so new test software reaches production safely and traceably.
* Build monitoring and alerting across factory infrastructure, and lead debugging when infrastructure issues block production.
* Integrate with contract manufacturers' factory systems (MES/SFIS) and with shared internal data platforms.
* Automate repetitive debug work, such as gathering evidence and grouping repeated failure signatures, and help build toward AI-assisted failure triage.

**You may be a good fit if you have (Must-have qualifications)**

* 3+ years of experience building and operating production infrastructure.
* Strong Linux administration skills: boot process, package management, systemd, storage, and debugging from the command line.
* Solid networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, VPNs, and how networks are laid out in server rooms or datacenters.
* Experience with distributed systems: services that run across many machines and keep working when some of them fail.
* Strong coding skills in Python, C++, or Rust. You build real tools and services, not only configuration.
* Experience with automation and configuration management (e.g. Ansible, Terraform) and CI/CD.
* Experience with monitoring and observability tools (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana) and debugging production issues.
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
* Willingness to work onsite in San Jose or Taiwan and travel to manufacturing partners as needed.

**Strong candidates may also have experience with (Nice-to-have qualifications)**

* Bare-metal server fleets, lab or datacenter automation, or HPC clusters (e.g. PXE, Slurm).
* Server management interfaces such as BMC, IPMI, or Redfish.
* Manufacturing test infrastructure, test automation platforms, or factory software (MES, SFIS).
* Data pipelines for test results, yield analysis, or hardware genealogy.
* AI servers, GPU or accelerator systems, or other high-performance compute platforms.
* Working with contract manufacturers; Mandarin is a plus for Taiwan-based candidates.
* Bringing first-generation hardware into production at a fast-paced startup.

**Benefits**

* Competitive compensation packages including generous equity packages
* Comprehensive insurance coverage and other top-of-market benefits

**How we’re different**

Etched believes in the Bitter Lesson. We are the first inference-focused frontier AI system. Our addressable market is the entirety of inference, unlike many of our competitors.

We are a fully in-person team in San Jose and Taipei, and greatly value engineering skills. We do not have boundaries between engineering and research, and we expect all of our technical staff to contribute to both as needed.

**Background**
